ov: Parasitic arachnids, related to mites, that feed on the blood of mammals, birds and sometimes reptiles and amphibians. Adults are 3–5 mm long but swell when they feed. Because they drink blood from host after host, they spread many serious diseases.

why.dg: Ticks spread serious diseases, such as Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis.

rg: Worldwide, especially in warm, humid climates; ticks even feed on penguins in Antarctica.
df: Blood only, from mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians.
fx: Larval ticks hatch with six legs and get their last pair after their first blood meal.
Ticks can survive in a near vacuum for as long as half an hour.
